directAnswer: To change the Windows lock screen, go to Settings > Personalization > Lock screen and select your desired background and options.
summary: Changing the Windows lock screen allows you to customize the appearance of your device when it's locked.

sections.heading: Customizing the Background
sections.body: You can choose a picture, a slideshow, or Windows Spotlight for your lock screen background.

sections.heading: Additional Settings
sections.body: You can also select apps to show quick status updates on your lock screen, such as calendar or email notifications.

steps.title: Open Settings
steps.detail: Click on the Start menu and select 'Settings' (gear icon).

steps.title: Navigate to Personalization
steps.detail: In the Settings window, click on 'Personalization'.

steps.title: Select Lock Screen
steps.detail: From the left-hand menu, click on 'Lock screen'.

steps.title: Choose Your Background
steps.detail: Under 'Background', select your preferred option (Picture, Slideshow, or Windows Spotlight) and configure any additional settings.

faqs.question: Can I use my own photos for the lock screen?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can select a personal photo by choosing 'Picture' under the background settings and browsing for your image.

faqs.question: Does changing the lock screen affect the login screen?
faqs.answer: No, the lock screen and login screen can be customized separately in Windows settings.

faqs.question: How do I revert to the default lock screen?
faqs.answer: To revert to the default lock screen, go back to the lock screen settings and select 'Windows Spotlight' or the default picture.

caveats: Some options may vary depending on your version of Windows (e.g., Windows 10 vs. Windows 11).
